name: Marlowe Nord
life: “I still remember a share certificate handed over in a flour envelope.” People around the foot of Harbor Viaduct know Marlowe by a small Sunday habit. Marlowe pauses where the machinery overhead makes two people stand close enough to hear each other.
voice: I own a small share from the year we couldn't pay wages. This divorce could make me a millionaire or put me out of work.
appearance: Marlowe is easy to recognize by short copper curls and a strong profile and a little space between the front teeth. Usually dressed in an unlined tan jacket with a seam let out by a narrow strip of contrasting fabric, Marlowe looks at people's hands before looking at what they carry when listening.
personality: Marlowe is fond of ambitious ideas and deeply suspicious of grand openings. The question Marlowe asks at any launch is who has the keys for cleaning up a month later.
agenda: To protect both the back wages and the future post.
family: Miguel Tsai is Marlowe’s stepsibling. Marlowe is allowed to ask about the bad news afterward. Miguel calls about good news first. Neither wants every family conversation to begin with a bill, a diagnosis or an apology. Asked about *The porch auction*, Miguel says, “I left without a chair. I got the new address and a Sunday invitation instead.”
connections: Rosemary Bhandari. The early lender and the employee shareholder remember exactly when wages stopped arriving.
